memory_candidates.content: When re-checking a single-observation deploy defect for reproducibility (e.g. a content-lossy config merge across two identical --wipe runs), use `jq -S` (sorted-key semantic diff) alongside the raw diff to distinguish genuine content loss from mere object-key/array-element ordering non-determinism. A raw multi-line diff that looks like whole blocks were dropped and relocated can be fully explained by non-deterministic key ordering (e.g. Lua table iteration leaking into JSON encoding) with `jq -S` on both sides showing zero semantic difference. Do not conclude content loss from a raw diff alone -- confirm with a sorted-key structural comparison first.

For a RECORDING-only gate task (fixes nothing structural, only records findings and spawns follow-ups), the sanctioned task-creation path can be replicated directly via state-write.sh using the exact schema /task's Create Task Mode documents (prepend to active_projects, increment next_project_number, pass --regen-todo) without needing the interactive /task command itself. This lets an implementer spawn multiple follow-up tasks in one dispatch while still going through the mutex-guarded, validated write path -- never a raw jq assignment to state.json.
